Once a Roman settlement, later a flourishing port, Bordeaux carries its centuries with effortless grace. The city’s boulevards and neoclassical facades earned it the affectionate name “La Petite Paris”—the Little Paris—though today it shines with its distinct brilliance.

Step into the Place de la Bourse, where stone and sky converse in the water’s reflection, and you feel history leaning gently toward the present. Beyond the city, vineyards spill across the landscape, weaving vintners' stories into wines celebrated worldwide.

A UNESCO World Heritage site, Bordeaux is more than a destination: it is a stage where architecture, history, and the art of wine entwine into something timeless.

あと、

美味しかったなぁ。また食べたい。

今回は、
世界も認めてる黄帝心仙人さんのアニメーションをMAZZELEのメンバーがチャレンジ！

今までのDJ DEKKAはスクラッチがうまくいかなかったり、
ちょいちょいミスはしてたんですが…

Project by M.Arch student Vandana Taluru (vandanashekar) for John Enright's (john_enright) Fall 2023 Vertical Studio.

Learn more about SCI-Arc Graduate Programs at the link in bio.

HOUSING RECAST
The project constitutes a critical examination of the architectural typology of single-family homes that gained prominence in the post-World War II era.

Within each 3D print bed, four residential structures are arranged to include one or two bedrooms. The drawings showcase a dynamic arrangement of volumes with walls curving the plan and section to create dynamic interior spaces as well as intimate outdoor spaces. Most walls are shared between units to optimise the quantity of material used.

The 3D-printed concrete walls reach a height of 12 feet, coupled with a dynamic metallic roofing system that envelops and tops the structure. Additionally, the incorporation of pre-fabricated utility pods represents a strategic and logistical intervention in the design. These pods are integrated into the overall neighborhood layout, adhering to a linear organization. This organizational schema serves the dual purpose of optimizing Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) services while mitigating the intrusion of utilityV conduits into the concrete structures.

In addition to these technical considerations, the dwellings are designed to afford each unit its own private courtyard. This feature contributes to the provision of intimate and personalized outdoor spaces for the inhabitants.

Quantitatively, each home is approximately 750sft of built space(Including the utilities pod) and has an additional 150sft of open yard.

🔎 Middle Mesial Canal Case: From Clue ➜ Canal ➜ Seal
Hidden MMCs can make or break retreatment success, this mandibular molar needed careful detective work.

1️⃣ Clues: Wide MB–ML distance and a subtle groove on the chamber floor hinted at an extra canal.
2️⃣ Locate: Microscope + gentle ultrasonic troughing ≤2 mm between MB–ML; NaOCl bubbles revealed the orifice.
3️⃣ Negotiate: Pre-curved #6–10 SS files (watch-wind) + EAL to confirm WL.
4️⃣ Shape: Conservative taper, protect the mesial “danger zone.”
5️⃣ Clean and Seal: Irrigant activation and 3D obturation for a dense fill.

💡 Missed canals = missed healing.

It has been ten years since we first ventured into Colombia. One incident that always comes to mind is our friend’s phone being snatched away as he was trying to make a call. Life was somewhat tougher back then, as the country was still recovering from a devastating coffee rust that swept through the nation. We were standing in the outskirts of the town Popayán, where the Ruiz brothers, Julian and Jairo, had just set up their new warehouse. It was our first time meeting each other, and it was a friendship that has lasted until today.

Until 2016, many of the leftist guerrilla groups like FARC and ELN relied on income from the lucrative drug trade to fund their operations. This inevitably led many coffee producers to switch towards the easier and higher-value coca cultivation. Over the years, we were continually reminded that certain regions were not safe for us to visit due to violence or the presence of the drug trade. Nonetheless, it never deterred us from being curious about this magical country and its people, as we continued exploring regions outside of the usual Cauca, Huila, and Nariño.

This year, we took part in the Subasta por la Paz 2025 (Auction for Peace) held in Bolívar, a small town south of the Cauca department. This was not just another coffee auction; it was a social event focused on farming sustainability and peace-building. Coffee acts as a catalyst, bringing producers and buyers from all around the world together to create a positive and hopefully lasting impact on the many lives involved with coffee. News of this event spread across communities, and producers were eager to submit their fresh harvests for the new year, hoping to land the top spot as the No.1 coffee in the department. The auction was lively, with the entire town and many from surrounding areas joining in to share the excitement and to see who would be this year’s winners.

Strap in. Three heady Dark Stars on this day. Here are your September 10th highlights...

1991 / MSG (30 Trips Box Set) - The funk was thick and the jams were deep. I was fortunate enough to have seen two of Branford Marsalis’ guest performances with the Grateful Dead, 3/29/90 at Nassau and this show on 9/10/91 at MSG. Both are among my favorite shows I attended. Thanks to Christopher Hazard c0nund4um for the video remaster 

1974 / London (Dave’s Picks #7) - Contemplative Star > Spam Jam > Apocalyptic Dew

“Unwinding very gently a la 11/11/73, the band circles around the song’s main frame for a few minutes before each member begins to fade into space. The gracefulness between each brief transition is breathtaking as it becomes evident that the sensory intuition level of the band is approaching its maximum facility level. Indeed, as each instrumentalist begins to stray into space, he is met at the destination by his colleagues. Lesh assumes the wheel, and the jam quickly accelerates to jazz mode, complemented by Godchaux’s finest Herbie Hancock “In a Silent Way” licks to date. The band returns to the theme and verse at twenty minutes. After a second meltdown, the “Star” quickly ascends from the ashes into a paranoia jam, a trifle funkier than usual, and certainly bordering on orgasmic. After several attempts to overthrow the playful interplay of feedback screams from Weir, Godchaux and Lesh authoritatively bring the jam to an instantaneous halt. As Godchaux spirals in calculated precision beneath Lesh’s pointed bomb dropping, the jam slowly melts, setting the path for the transition into “Morning Dew.” The Dead ascertain the spiritual conclusion of the voyage.” ~ Brian Dyke, The Deadheads Taping Compendium, Volume 1 (1959-1974)

Author: Kristen Ashley 
Pub. Date: September 9, 2025

Thank you, kristenashleybooks, 1001darknights_blueboxpress and getredprbooks for my copy!

Review:

Blake and Dair have known each other since they were kids, and as adults, they’re not exactly each other’s biggest fans. Blair sees Dair as a bully, and Dair thinks Blair is a spoiled brat. But disliking each other doesn’t stop the sparks from flying—and wow, the chemistry is instant and intense.

Finding the One really feels like a redemption story for Blair, who we first met in earlier books with a bit of a mean girl reputation. This time, though, we get to see her layers, and I absolutely loved her character. She’s the kind of heroine I always root for—the underestimated one who struggles with her own self-image, making her growth and glow-up that much more powerful and emotional.

And then there’s Dair. He’s pure KA alpha male, complete with an accent, and trust me—you’ll swoon. The story even throws in some third-act drama, which honestly made me happy because it led to an epic mea culpa and a reunion that had me cracking up.

The family drama is juicy enough to rival a soap opera, and the hurdles this couple faces make their determination to stick together even more powerful. They discover that their true strength comes from leaning on each other. And romance readers, you’re in for a treat—the spice levels are scorching!

If you’re into redemption arcs, messy family dynamics, and a romance that brings both heat and heart, this book delivers.

Long road trips with kids don’t have to mean endless screens. We did a 7 hour road trip with our (almost) 4 year old, and here are some things that really helped us:

1️⃣ Save the screen-free travel activities for later in the trip (don’t hand them out right away!)

2️⃣ Pack plenty of healthy road trip snacks to keep blood sugar balanced

3️⃣ Plan movement breaks — kids need 10–15 minutes to run, stretch, and reset before hopping back in the car

Honestly, sitting that long is tough for little kids, but with the right mix of activities, snacks, and stops, I felt it was totally doable. And if you end up using screens for some parts of it, save it towards the end!

New studies show metabolism doesn’t actually slow down with age. So, what’s actually going on?

It all comes down to muscle.

The greatest single influence on your metabolic rate is how much muscle you have. Muscle mass decreases approximately 3–8% per decade after the age of 35 if you’re not doing anything to proactively MAINTAIN and BUILD it.

Age-related muscle loss has a massive ripple effect. As you lose it, you become more insulin resistant. This causes poor blood sugar control, fatigue, chronic inflammation, and hormonal shifts, like high cortisol and low estrogen.

Studies show the solution is simple: protect your muscle to prevent decline.

WHAT CAN YOU DO? As you age, you need to eat MORE protein to initiate muscle protein synthesis. Your body is continually breaking down protein and building new protein throughout the day. 

Women 40+ need an additional 10-15g per meal than younger adults to stimulate muscle growth! Without it, muscle loss is inevitable.

Another key player? Micro movements. After 40, research shows people move less—less taking the stairs, less walk breaks, less mobility work, less chasing after kids. This shift in movement slowly leads to greater fragility, pain, and loss of strength.

Muscle is your built-in defense plan.

If you want to protect your metabolism, brain, and blood sugar as you age, make muscle your #1 priority.

INVESTIDORES AMERICANOS ASSUMIRÃO OPERAÇÕES 

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, assinou nesta quinta (25) uma ordem executiva que define novo acordo para o TikTok no país, garantindo que investidores norte-americanos assumam o controle da operação. 

A Oracle será a principal responsável pela segurança da plataforma, enquanto empresários como Michael Dell e Rupert Murdoch também participarão do negócio.

Trump afirmou ter chegado a um entendimento com o presidente chinês Xi Jinping e destacou que a operação será tributada nos EUA. 

Já o vice-presidente JD Vance disse que a versão americana da rede social deve ser avaliada em cerca de US$ 14 bilhões, oferecendo mais estabilidade aos usuários.

👉🏻 Diesel SS26 沒有傳統的時裝秀，而是在米蘭的街頭散佈了 34 顆蛋：酒吧、教堂、馬路邊都能看到。裡頭則站著身穿最新系列的模特兒們！

👉🏻 只要上 Diesel 網站就會給你一個動態地圖，而所有人都能透過地圖去「獵蛋」 (Egg Hunt)！

👉🏻 這場比賽吸引 5000 人參賽，而最快搜集完所有蛋的人則能獲得 Diesel 訂製的服裝和包款作為獎品！

👉🏻 這就讓人想到 Glenn Martens 這個月在訪談中提到的「時尚變成了『飢餓遊戲』」的言論！

👉🏻 透過 Diesel 他試圖打破「時尚只服務部份人」的天花板，讓所有人都能參與，不分性別、年齡、職業！

👉🏻 同時他也不忘 Diesel 的核心：翻轉丹寧。緞面的丹寧、印花皮革、解構大衣，持續在服裝設計上突破！

Glenn Martens 在不壓縮深度與細節的理想上，用充滿實驗性的方式說故事，同時讓每一個人都能享受時尚。他說「Diesel 談的是民主，它的本質是一個生活品牌。」這個理想，就貫徹著他的每一個決策。

Perché trovare un jeans giusto sembra sempre più difficile?

Comprare un jeans dovrebbe essere semplice, e invece è un esercizio di pazienza.
Online non puoi capire come cade, come accompagna i movimenti, come dialoga con le scarpe. E per essere certa che almeno un paio funzioni, spesso dovresti ordinarne almeno 10.

In negozio, il tempo è poco, le luci non aiutano e finiamo per provarlo solo con le calzature che abbiamo addosso in quel momento. Per poi non sapere come sta con le altre.

➡️ A complicare le cose ci si mettono le differenze di brand, di fit, di lavaggi: quello che sembra perfetto in camerino, spesso a casa delude. Così negli armadi si accumulano jeans “quasi giusti”, indossati solo quando non ci sono alternative migliori.

Eppure basterebbe osservare pochi elementi chiave – cavallo, orlo, tasche – per evitare la maggior parte di questi errori.

➡️ E poi c’è un dettaglio che raramente consideriamo: la composizione. 
Un denim senza elastane ha una resa migliore, mantiene la forma, dura di più. E ha un fitting migliore, c’è poco da fare. Quell’effetto elasticizzato all’inizio sembra più comodo, ma col tempo cede, si deforma, crea piccole onde dove la linea dovrebbe restare netta.

La verità è che non serve comprare di più, ma scegliere con più attenzione. 
Osservare i dettagli che fanno la differenza. 
Camminare, sedersi, piegarsi. 

Perché un jeans non deve solo “stare bene” davanti allo specchio: deve funzionare nella vita reale.

Nuovo dress code a scuola: davvero il problema sono le caviglie?
Possiamo dircelo senza giri di parole: la crociata sui centimetri di pelle è il modo più pigro per far finta di parlare di educazione. A chi serve? A chi controlla i corpi, non a chi deve imparare.

Polemica sì, ma con logica:

Se “decoro” è la parola d’ordine, valga per tuttə: studenti, docenti, staff. La prima cosa da dire che o c'è coerenza o è solo moralismo.

E parliamo di “Concentrazione”: chi si distrae per una spalla scoperta ha bisogno di educazione all’attenzione, non di regole da collegio 1950.

Infine, lo sappiamo tutti chi viene fermato più spesso al corridoio. Se il regolamento colpisce soprattutto le ragazze qua stiamo parlando di polizia del corpo.

Per il resto sono d'accordo sul fatto che la scuola deve insegnare responsabilità, contesto, rispetto—non far passare il messaggio che la colpa è del tuo top.
Vuoi davvero migliorare il clima d’aula? Parla di come si sta insieme: linguaggio, confini, ascolto, uso dei telefoni, puntualità.
E le regole ci vogliono? Sì: poche, chiare, co-create, misurate sul benessere e la sicurezza, non sulla vergogna.

Io scelgo una scuola che educa la testa, non che misura l’orlo.

(però diciamocelo: alcune persone si vestono in modo poco opportuno...)

Che ne pensi?

👉  Seguimi su giovannifenu.memovia per sapere ogni giorno più degli altri

🚀  Scrivi INFO per sapere come funziona il Corso di Apprendimento Fenomenico e impara a studiare velocemente, a perfezione e senza ansia... Alla prima lettura (senza metodi assurdi come rileggere, sottolineare, schematizzare e ripetere)

What’s your favorite track from Rahsaan Patterson’s self-titled debut (1997)?

Released on MCA in early ’97, Rahsaan’s first album was a critic’s gem — praised for its honesty, musicianship, and a vocal style often compared to Stevie Wonder. Backed by producers Keith Crouch, Jamey Jaz, and Ira Schickman, the sound was warm and live-leaning: keys, bass, grooves, and space for Rahsaan’s elastic tenor to glide.

Singles Stop By and Where You Are didn’t explode on the Hot 100 but left their mark — both charting on R&B radio and even finding life overseas in the UK. Where You Are first appeared on the Bulletproof soundtrack (1996) before landing here, while Stop By showcased his falsetto power on R&B airwaves.

By the time this album dropped, Rahsaan already had receipts: he co-wrote Brandy’s breakout hit Baby in 1994, proving he could pen smashes before stepping into his own spotlight. And while commercial success was modest, the album built his cult following — heads still regard it as one of the purest expressions of late-90s soul.

Drop your standout from the album below, and tell us: which project should be next on our underrated R&B list? (For context, #5 was Zhané’s Saturday Night and #4 was Donell Jones’ Life Goes On.)

📸La conservación de las aves y el talento fotográfico colombiano se hicieron sentir en la más reciente edición de los Premios de Fotografía Audubon 2025, donde cuatro fotógrafos colombianos, entre ellos un bugueño de 14 años, fueron reconocidos entre miles de participantes internacionales.

🇨🇴Los galardonados fueron Luis Alberto Peña, Camilo Sanabria Grajales, Cristian Valencia y Shamir Shah, quienes se destacaron en distintas categorías con imágenes que, según el jurado, combinan destreza técnica, sensibilidad artística y un fuerte mensaje de conservación.

🏙️ Shah se llevó el premio en Aves en el Paisaje, Colombia, por su retrato de loros jaboneros (Blue-headed Parrots) en Cali, integrados al verdor de la vegetación. (Foto #2)

🐦Sanabria, por su parte, ganó el Premio Juventud gracias a la extraordinaria captura de un Blackburnian Warbler (reinita gorginaranja) cazando una polilla. (Foto #3)

🌺Valencia fue reconocido en la categoría Plantas para las Aves, Colombia, con una fotografía de un colibrí Purple-backed Thornbill alimentándose de flores nativas en los bosques de Villamaría, Caldas. (Foto #4)

🦅Finalmente, Peña obtuvo el Premio Conservación con una impactante fotografía de un gavilán cerca de un incendio auto provocado en una zona rural de Cúcuta. (Fotos #1 y 5)

Apa yang biasanya kamu lakukan pas lagi bertengkar dengan pasangan? Membicarakan langsung masalah tersebut meskipun dengan penuh emosi atau justru mendiamkan pasanganmu?

And so what would he ask? What would he want? The Batman: Part II

Matt Reeves said early on that every idea was on the table, even Robin. “Well sure you talk about everything. There is probably not any character that we didn’t talk about. What could this be? What could that be? That’s part of the beginning of anything.” A major focus was the villain, and Reeves teased a new angle: “Picking the right villain that digs into his past and his life… I will say it’s never really been done in a movie before.”

This time, the film will lean more into Bruce Wayne. “One of the explorations for me was to do something that pushes even further into the character of Bruce Wayne because the first story is so much about The Batman. I never wanted to lose [Robert Pattinson] at the center of these stories.”

The script has already impressed the cast. Colin Farrell praised it, saying, “The script is unbelievable. It’s so good. God, Matt Reeves, it’s so good. It really is. It’s extraordinary.” Reeves also shared Robert Pattinson’s reaction after reading: “He’s Batman, so if he doesn’t like it, not good… the fact that he did was incredibly encouraging.”

With the script finished, the film is officially in pre-production. Reeves confirmed, “We’re beginning. We’re staffing up. We’re starting to get our crew back together. We’re basically entering pre-production. We’ll be making the movie in the spring… super excited.” He also promised, “I really do think this movie will be better than the last. [Robert Pattinson] feels that way.”

Reeves closed with a tease for fans: “I feel so honored to be preparing to shoot the Next Chapter of our story… Can’t wait to share lots of exciting things about the movie with you all in the weeks and months to come.”

Sharing the court with RogerFederer, the greatest of all time and my favourite tennis player since I was a kid, was a literal dream come true. It was an incredible day of doubles with Roger and TommyHaasOfficial on one of the most beautiful courts I have ever stepped foot on.

I told Roger that the first tennis match I ever went to was when my dad took me to the Rogers Cup in Toronto in 2006 to watch him play Gasquet in the final. Roger remembered the match immediately - it was a close one where Gasquet won the first set and had several break opportunities in the second before Roger rallied to win in three. That day solidified my love for tennis (and for Federer), and I’m still pinching myself that I got the opportunity to play with (and against) a world number one and number two! I told Roger that I’ve had actual dreams about this, and his response was “Was this match better or worse than the one in your dreams?” 😂

Roger and Tommy, thank you both so much for your kindness, graciousness, for all the tips and for an awesome match! This is a memory I will cherish forever. I also appreciate your patience with my relentless rush to volley everything. I’m glad Tommy and I pulled out the hard-fought win there on match point hahaha. 🏆🎾

For the past year, we have been working on the second issue of our in-house magazine, Freedom Hill magazine.

When I say “we”, I mean a collective of around 20 people located all around the world, with a common interest in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu and its culture.
In the era of digital, why making a magazine?

Because it’s meaningful for us. Every pictures taken, articles written are carefully chosen and cared for.
A magazine is not eternal like a book. It’s meant to be carried around, read on the corner of a table and forgotten in a pile somewhere…but it serves as a powerful link to culture itself. It captures on paper a bit of the passion we have for something.

For the cover of this issue (it will be released on October first), we had the honor to work with Meisa Fujishiro, a renowned Japanese photographer and BJJ practitioner. I wanted him to photograph his son Ryunosuke who trains BJJ with us in Jiyugaoka.

I am really interested in the bonds that BJJ creates between people especially the connection between different generations and cultures. I like to think members of a dojo as interconnected through BJJ.

The mag will be available on October 1st, at Carpe Diem BJJ Jiyugaoka and through the Carpe Diem BJJ online store.

Picture by Meisa Fujishiro meisafujishiro 

この1年間、私たちは社内誌『Freedom Hill Magazine』の第2号に取り組んできました。
「私たち」と言うとき、それは世界中に散らばる約20人の仲間を指します。私たちは皆、ブラジリアン柔術とその文化への共通の情熱でつながっています。

デジタル時代に、なぜ雑誌を作るのか？
それは、私たちにとって意味があるからです。撮影された写真も、書かれた記事も、すべて丁寧に選び、心を込めて作っています。

雑誌は本のように永遠ではありません。テーブルの片隅で読まれ、どこかの山に埋もれてしまうかもしれません。ですが、文化と強く結びつく存在です。私たちが抱く情熱の一部を、紙の上に固定することができるのです。

今回の号（10月1日発売予定）の表紙では、日本の著名な写真家であり、BJJの実践者でもある藤代冥砂さんとご一緒することができました。藤代さんの息子で、自由が丘で一緒にBJJを練習している藤代龍之介くんを撮影していただきました。

私は、BJJが人と人をつなぐ力にとても興味があります。特に、世代や文化を超えたつながりです。道場の仲間は、BJJを通して互いにつながっている存在だと考えています。

この雑誌は、10月1日からカルペディエムBJJ自由が丘、そしてカルペディエムBJJオンラインストアで入手可能です。

Existem diversas traduções desse poema seminal de Forugh Farrokhzad, alguns com o título “Apenas a voz ficará”, outros intitulados “Apenas o som ficará”. Ele está disponível no terceiro volume da publicação educativa da 36ª Bienal de São Paulo, elaborado a partir da Invocação #3, 'Mawali-Taqsim: Improvisação como espaço e tecnologia da humanidade', que aconteceu em Zanzibar, em fevereiro de 2025.

Farrokhzad foi uma poeta e autora modernista nascida em Teerã, reconhecida por sua postura feminista e por desafiar as convenções sociais de sua época. Sua obra explorou o desejo feminino, a sensualidade e as restrições culturais impostas às mulheres, oferecendo voz às experiências íntimas e emocionais das mulheres em sua sociedade. 

[𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗟𝗜𝗦𝗛] "A bird long dead counseled me to remember flight" – Forugh Farrokhzad, poet. There are various translations of this seminal poem, some titled “Only Voice Remains,” others “Only Sound Remains”. It is part of the second volume of the 36th Bienal’s educational publication, based on the Invocation #3, 'Mawali-Taqsim: Improvisation as a Space and Technology of Humanity', which took place in Zanzibar in February 2025.

Forugh Farrokhzad was a modernist poet and author born in Tehran, recognized for her feminist stance and for challenging the social conventions of her time. Her work explored female desire, sensuality, and the cultural restrictions imposed on women, giving voice to the intimate and emotional experiences of women in her society.

📕 Forugh Farrokhzad, 'Sin: Selected Poems of Forugh Farrokhzad' (University of Arkansas Press, 2008). Tradução para o inglês / Translation to English: Sholeh Wolpé. Traduzido para o português / Translation to Portuguese: Alexandre Barbosa de Souza.

What does it mean to confront the memories of a nation scarred by war — and to find new ways of seeing beyond its silences?

𝘈𝘧𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘈𝘱𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘢𝘴 brings together six pioneering Sri Lankan artists — Anoli Perera (anoliperera ), Chandraguptha Thenuwara (chandragupthathenuwara ), Jagath Weerasinghe (jagathweerasinghe ), Kingsley Gunatillake (kingsleygunatillake ), Muhanned Cader (muhannedcader ), and Pala Pothupitiye (palapothupitiye ) — who in the 1990s forged a visual language that challenged state narratives of power and reshaped how the experience of violence could be articulated in the public sphere. 

In 𝘏𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘴 𝘞𝘳𝘢𝘱𝘱𝘦𝘥 𝘪𝘯 𝘊𝘭𝘰𝘵𝘩, 𝘉𝘰𝘳𝘥𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘙𝘢𝘪𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘪𝘯 𝘍𝘭𝘢𝘨𝘴, Hema Shironi (shironijoseph ) turns fabric, thread, and found material into meditations on how histories, memories, and identities are layered unequally in the aftermath of war. Grappling with her own struggle to locate her lived experience within multi-generational histories, Shironi pushes us to acknowledge many truths of Tamilness and Sinhalaness — tethered to land, blood, and memory — even as she insists on the possibility of hope.

Together, the two exhibitions ask audiences to reckon with Sri Lanka’s violent past while opening space for shared futures.

𝘈𝘧𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘈𝘱𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘢𝘴 and 𝘏𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘴 𝘞𝘳𝘢𝘱𝘱𝘦𝘥 𝘪𝘯 𝘊𝘭𝘰𝘵𝘩, 𝘉𝘰𝘳𝘥𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘙𝘢𝘪𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘪𝘯 𝘍𝘭𝘢𝘨𝘴, presented by Shrine Empire (shrineempire), are #OnView at Bikaner House, New Delhi, until September 25.

MEINE TOP TWELVE 👶🏼🫧 Diesen Beitrag habt ihr euch so häufig gewünscht, also kommen hier meine ganz persönlichen Favoriten in puncto Erstausstattung. Es geht immer mehr oder weniger, ist von Baby zu Baby und auch von Jahreszeit zu Jahreszeit unterschiedlich, aber diese Produkte sind hier on high rotation. 

#1 Bodies, Bodies, Bodies – oder Strampler sind gerade an „Zuhause-Tagen“ oftmals das ganze Outfit und kann man nie genug haben.

#2 Selbiges gilt für Musselintücher. Als Spuck- oder Stilltuch, Decke, Sonnenschutz etc. Bei uns ständig im Einsatz. 

#3 Unsere Babywippe kommt überall mit hin. War bei Baby 1, 2 und 3 gleichermaßen beliebt.

#4 Genauso wie unsere Babytragen, unsere beiden Favoriten sind von artipoppe und flybaby.berlin.

#5 Bei uns ist im Bad kein Platz, aber wir lieben unseren schönen Wickelplatz mit Stauraum, der später als Kommode weitergenutzt werden kann, ohnehin. Tipp: Die Wickelauflage Matty von leander.furniture.

DEAR MAMA OVER 370 MILLION STREAMS ON SPOTIFY

2Pac's "Dear Mama" has reached over 370 million streams on Spotify. This occured just yesterday Sunday on September 21, 2025. 

Undoubtedly one of the greatest rap song ever dedicated to mothers. It remains one of 2Pac’s most iconic, celebrated, and referenced tracks of all time. Countless rappers have drawn inspiration from this heartfelt tribute. It offers a deep look into his early life and his honest, genuine bond with his mother. This timeless classic will always remind us to love, cherish, and be forever grateful to our mothers. Mom, you are appreciated. 

2pac recorded "Dear Mama" featuring. Sweet Franklin & Reggie Green in "Studio B" at Encore Studios, 721 South Glenwood Place in Burbank, California on July 14, 1994. According to the reels information, it was engineered by Tony Pizarro together and assistant engineered by Carlos Warlick. The reel was titled "E-8" and consisted of two recorded tracks; "Dear Mama (Main)" with chorus and "Dear Mama (No Lady Mix" without chorus. The original version was produced by dj_master_tee and was recorded at Unique Recording Studios in or around October of 1993.

It was released as the debut and lead single from Pac's third album "Me Against the World". On March 11, 1995 "Dear Mama" topped at #1 on billboard "Hot Rap Songs" and peaked at #9 on the Billboard ”Hot 100” on April 29, 1995. It spent five weeks on chart. The single was certified Platinum on July 13, 1995 with 1 million copies sold by the riaa_awards.

Tuesday, September 4, 1973. Santiago, Chile. A day to remember: the Third Anniversary of the President Allende UP government. 
Fifty-three years ago the Left democratically voted for President Allende. They’d voted for a better life and won. In the intervening years, life had not been easy: the UP government had Nationalized the Chile copper mines, banks and factories, etc. In retaliation the US government increased sanctions on the country, and many imported items became scarce or unavailable. But in the next three years “El Pueblo” had a little more food on the table, a half-liter of milk daily for every child and a little more justice and equality. Today ‘El Pueblo’ came together to celebrate that momentous occasion: they came by the thousands, by train, by bus, by truckload and on foot. The streets were packed. They were happy. This was their day, their victory, they were everywhere in the center of Santiago: over a hundred thousand people. Together they chanted, ‘Allende, Allende el pueblo te defiende.” Yes it was a day to remember. 
#1 Hundreds cheered President Allende on his way to work that morning. 
#2 #18 By late afternoon the plaza in front of the Moneda Palace and the surrounding streets were filled with thousands of people singing and chanting.
 #6 Photographers and cameramen line up to have their turn of taking a birds-eye picture of the immense crowd celebrating.
#19 The huge land owners had been forced give up some of their land, this peasant-farmer had received a small parcel and for first time had grown potatoes on his own land. He wanted to thank President Allende: with a bag of potatoes. But the bag was too heavy to lift. The President took one potato as acknowledgment of his gift.

Presentamos una noche dedicada a Kind of Blue, la obra maestra de Miles Davis y uno de los discos más influyentes en la historia del jazz.

El evento contará con la participación de Chema Hernández (chemasoficial), melómano y periodista, apasionado del jazz y colaborador habitual en las sesiones de escucha de Red Luna.

Exploraremos el contexto histórico del álbum: su importancia dentro de la carrera de Miles Davis, la genialidad de los músicos que lo acompañaron y la manera en que definió el sonido del jazz modal.

Después, escucharemos el vinilo en la increíble sala de El Q4RTO, un espacio diseñado para una experiencia auditiva inmersiva.

Esta sesión forma parte de las experiencias de escucha organizadas por Red Luna Producciones, con el objetivo de ofrecer espacios únicos para explorar y profundizar en la historia de la música, permitiendo una conexión más cercana con los discos.

Psycho Circus Was Released September 22 1998

Produced by Bruce Fairbairn. Recorded at One On One Studios and A&M Studios in Los Angeles, CA, January - April 1998. Final mastering completed 6/24/98 by George Marino. Strings arranged by Shelly Berg.  Drums on all of the album's tracks, except "Into The Void," were performed by Kevin Valentine. The majority of the lead guitar work was by Tommy Thayer (apparently offered some $20K for the effort) with some having the sonic signature of Paul Stanley (but not necessarily being by him). Some notes indicate that Bruce Kulick played bass on "Psycho Circus" and "Body And Soul;" and it is likely that there are other contributions by him.

Performance credits:

Psycho Circus - Bruce Kulick on bass; Tommy Thayer on lead guitar
We Are One - Tommy Thayer on bass and guitars; Gene Simmons on acoustic guitar
I Finally Found My Way - Bruce Kulick on bass; Shelly Berg on acoustic piano; Bob Ezrin on Fender Rhodes
I Pledge Allegiance - Bruce Kulick on bass on chorus; Paul Stanley guitar solo
Within - Bruce Kulick on backwards guitar intro (from demo)
You Wanted The Best - Ace Frehley on guitar solo
Raise Your Glasses - Paul Stanley guitar solo
Dreamin' - Bruce Kulick on bass
Journey Of 1,000 Years - Shelly Berg on acoustic piano

** It's pretty obvious that there are other players on the album, mainly Tommy Thayer (providing the majority of lead and rhythm guitars) and Kevin Valentine (drums). The only song on the album the original four members play on is "Into The Void"...

Chart Action:

Chart Peak: #3 (10/1/98) with 14 weeks on charts. Other countries: AUS #25; AUZ #1; CAN #2; GER #5; JAP #20; NOR #4; SWE #1; SWZ #30; UK #47.

RIAA/Sales:

"Psycho Circus" was certified gold by the RIAA on 10/22/98. By February 2007 the album had sold 481,000 according to SoundScan(r). It is currently out-of-print in the USA. By 2003 Universal Music International reported international sales of over 400,000 of the album (Billboard, 8/9/03).

The 8-Mile pack has only gray wolves right now, which is super cool! Usually we see about 50/50 in terms of coat color in the park. Gray wolves are a lot harder to spot on the landscape. They camouflage super well, especially amongst the sage brush. 8-Mile produced 8 puppies this year, and are doing well. They’re a pack that’s pretty tough to spot in Yellowstone, but it’s always such a treat to see them when we do. 

You’ll see some pups licking the joules of one of the adults in both video 2 and video 4. This pup is looking for a feeding! When pups lick the lips of an adult, they’re hoping that the wolf will regurgitate, or throw up, a meal 🤮

What’s your favorite song from this modern-day classic? 👇🏾

10 years ago today, Bryson Tiller released his debut album T R A P S O U L.

This was the project that shifted the sound of R&B in the mid-2010s. Before T R A P S O U L, R&B and hip-hop were already blending, but Tiller’s take gave the fusion a new identity. He took moody, atmospheric production, added sharp lyrical storytelling, and layered it with vocals that moved between rapping and singing. The result was a lane that artists are still trying to occupy a decade later.

The breakthrough single Don’t spread like wildfire online before the album even dropped. By the time the full project arrived, fans already knew they were hearing something fresh. Songs like Exchange and Sorry Not Sorry showed the vulnerability and rawness in his pen, while Overtime and Rambo carried the grit and confidence that made him more than just a singer. The balance between those energies became the heart of the album’s appeal.

Bryson’s delivery gave every track weight. His voice could sound wounded, reflective, and defiant all within the same verse. That emotional honesty helped a generation of listeners feel like their own late-night thoughts and heartbreaks finally had a soundtrack.

Commercially, the album debuted at #11 on the Billboard 200 and climbed to #8, eventually going Platinum. It earned him comparisons to Drake and The Weeknd, but instead of being lost in those shadows, T R A P S O U L carved out its own space. The record didn’t just ride the wave of moody R&B — it defined the wave.

Ten years later, the influence of T R A P S O U L is everywhere, from the sound of streaming-era R&B to the aesthetics of artists who came after. It turned Bryson Tiller from a Louisville kid uploading songs to SoundCloud into one of the most important voices of his generation.

當年還在訓練時的人生第一個過夜班就是羽田。當時很幸運地，和一位文藻的學妹一起飛，她就帶我到藍瓶子樓上的Sarabeth吃鬆餅。

每次羽田過夜班都會經過看到atré二樓的藍瓶子，但就是沒有上來喝個一杯咖啡。

這次原本想起個早床找間咖啡廳喝一杯咖啡，結果沒想到因為要跨年，幾乎所有的咖啡廳都要10點才開，唯一一間有開的咖啡廳被擠滿了人。

於是就去超商隨便亂採買甜點搭上飛機吃之後，就等到10點等藍瓶子開。

喝完傳說中的藍瓶子後，覺得

好像沒有比較厲害🤣

後來在機場的Curación買的冰滴咖啡，咖啡因強到我喝了整趟四小時的飛行，還兑了氣泡水才喝得下去。

雖然如此，還是不爭氣地買了一個藍瓶子隨行杯☕️

Anyways, 祝大家新年快樂！

KYOTO・抹茶腦袋的京都小確幸時光🍵🍃

📍#藍瓶咖啡 (京都六角店) bluebottlejapan 
「Blue Bottle Coffee 京都六角店」前身為百年町家「辻森自行車商會」，如今搖身一變成為結合咖啡與自行車文化的複合式空間。店內延續「Cycle Hub」概念，保留原有建築風貌，並提供自行車維修與租借服務，別具在地風格。

這裡還有⭐️限定販售的抹茶甜點，不定期輪替，有時是濃郁乳酪蛋糕、有時則是焦香巴斯克。若你同時是藍瓶咖啡迷與抹茶控，推薦特地安排時間過來坐坐，享受在充滿生活感的老屋裡，度過一場屬於京都的靜謐咖啡時光。

📍#8108kyoto / #八十八良葉舎 (清水店) 8108kyoto 
「八十八良葉舎」是一間專注於京都府產單品抹茶的日本茶專門店，創始店隱身於京都右京區嵯峨朝日町，位置較為隱密，需從京都搭電車前往嵐山途中，要在「車折神社」站下車。

令人欣喜的是，「八十八良葉舎」如今已拓展至嵐山旗艦店、清水店，以及東京淺草、鎌倉等地，即使身處熱門觀光區，也能輕鬆品嚐一杯香氣深遠、風味濃郁的抹茶飲品。
 其中「八十八良葉舎 清水店」就位在法觀寺八坂之塔旁、鄰近二年坂；若有計畫前往清水寺一帶，推薦熱愛抹茶的你，來這裡朝聖一杯真正來自京都產地的抹茶風味。

📍#茶和々 (錦市場) sawawa_kyoto 
「茶和々」在日本多地都有分店，每間皆主打不同造型的吸睛甜點，充滿趣味與創意。我這次來到的是京都錦市場門市；逛市場之餘，可以順道來杯冰涼茶飲或抹茶冰淇淋消暑一下！

📍#SNOOPY茶屋 (京都 錦店) snoopychaya_japan 
「SNOOPY 茶屋京都錦店」販售各式史努比主題周邊與造型甜點，從甜品到包裝都充滿可愛巧思。逛完錦市場、吃完中餐後，這裡適合當作稍作歇息的小站。

📍#伊藤久右衛門 (多間門市) itohkyuemon 
「伊藤久右衛門」是源自京都宇治的老字號抹茶品牌。除了宇治本店，在京都市區、大阪、東京淺草等觀光熱點也設有分店。沒時間內用的話，也很推薦外帶一杯抹茶漂浮拿鐵，濃郁茶香中帶點甜，是散步途中最療癒的小確幸。

Little tricks of „big“ climbs #2: While packing for an expedition these days I start to feel the good old excitement and it makes me think of what were usually recipes for a good expedition in my past. I came to the conclusion that after staying alive and healthy a very important factor was always connected with other teams or better said how to avoid them on the same objective. During my expeditions I always tried to stay away from the objectives I would need to share with other teams. Not because I don’t like people but because I realized that no mater the experience people’s decisions making tend to get more or less affected with other people on the same project. By my experience in a bad way. So my advice for everyone but also a reminder to myself is to be creative and find your peace out in the mountains. As an irony I am sharing photos from trips to Patagonia and India. In case of Patagonia we managed to stay totally alone on our objectives despite being in one of the more busy places in the main season. On the other side in 2014 in India in a very quiet place, we ended up being two parties below the north face of Hagshu with the aim to climb it (even exactly same line). We arrived just a week earlier than the other party realizing we won’t be alone when we were already in the town of Leh on the way to basecamp. We ended up climbing that line and the other party climbed a different one. You can read about a big disappointment and one side of the story in Mick Fowler‘s book. 11 years later I still 100% disagree with it. But this unpleasant situation definitely encouraged me even more to find objectives away from others. There are too many mountains/routes for one life anyway so why putting additional stress with dealing with other people’s plans.

Quais ortodontistas brasileiros produzem ciência com maior impacto científico?

Existem rankings e rankings, é verdade. 
Um dos mais respeitados para avaliar o impacto da ciência é o “c-score”, desenvolvido por pesquisadores da Stanford University em parceria com a editora Elsevier.
📈Essa métrica valoriza as citações que os cientistas recebem enquanto protagonistas de um artigo publicado (1° ou último autor). 
O c-score 2025 foi publicado esta semana. O nosso país apresenta um dos maiores números de ortodontistas entre os mais citados em 2024. São nove, entre oito docentes de universidades públicas de todas as regiões do país: norte (David Normando- UFPA), centro-oeste (Jorge Faber- UNB); nordeste (Matheus Pithon- UESB), sudeste (Guilherme Janson- USP in memoriam,  Daniela Garib- USP , Lucas Abreu- UFMG; Antônio Carlos Ruellas- UFRJ), e sul (Graziela Canto- UFSC), além da Profa Lúcia Cevidanes, atualmente na University of North Carolina.
Produzir e valorizar ciência de impacto é fundamental para desenvolvermos a nossa especialidade e o nosso país.

"Breach" ya se ha transformado en un nuevo hito para Twenty One Pilots . Además de haberse instalado en el Top 10 de las listas británicas, están celebrando un triunfo mayor en Estados Unidos: su nuevo disco debutó en el Número 1 del Billboard 200, el ranking más importante de álbumes en ese país.

El dúo conformado por Tyler Joseph y Josh Dun logra así su primer número uno desde el fenómeno global de Blurryface en 2015. Desde entonces, sus lanzamientos habían quedado muy cerca de la cima: Trench en el puesto #2, y tanto Scaled And Icy como Clancy en el #3. Ahora, con Breach, alcanzan nuevamente la cúspide después de casi una década de espera. En su primera semana, el disco vendió 200.000 unidades equivalentes de álbum, de las cuales 169.000 fueron ventas tradicionales (CDs, vinilos y descargas completas), un número realmente impresionante en la era del streaming.

Este logro no es menor: se trata de la semana más exitosa para un álbum de rock en Estados Unidos en los últimos seis años. El último en conseguir un impacto semejante había sido Fear Inoculum de Tool en 2019, lo que coloca a Breach en un lugar histórico.

 Según antecedentes recientes, encontramos a Paramore con This Is Why (#2 en 2023, pero sin alcanzar la cima), a Foo Fighters con Medicine at Midnight (#3 en 2021), y a Greta Van Fleet con Anthem of the Peaceful Army (#3 en 2018). Solo casos excepcionales, como Tool con Fear Inoculum (#1 en 2019), AC/DC con Power Up (#1 en 2020), Alabama Shakes con "Sound & Colors" (2015) o más atrás Foo Fighters con "Wasting Light" (#1 en 2011) habían logrado lo que ahora alcanza TØP.

Tyler Joseph compartió la emoción en su cuenta de X con un mensaje sincero y algo sorprendido: “Bueno… Breach fue #1. ¿Por qué esto me puso tan feliz que hasta se me salieron unas lágrimas? No muchas, solo un poco. Hace 10 años ni siquiera entendía lo que significaba un álbum número uno, pero desde Blurryface siempre quise repetirlo. Y nunca llegó. Luego dejé de desearlo y simplemente escribí un disco para ustedes. Para nosotros."

"REVELING IN BLUE #2" | 160 x 200 cm (79 x 63 in) | mixed media, hands and passion on raw canvas.

Swipe for a studio pic, interior example, early stages and some details. 

If you didn't see the post with "REVELING IN BLUE #2" here's a short explanation about the idea I started with:

Paintings come from many different sources of inspiration. Sometimes, like this one, they’re simply the result of enjoying the material and immersing myself in a single color.

My love for the material has always played an important role in my painting practice. That’s why this piece was created mostly with my hands, without using brushes or other tools. I only used them in the later stages to round off the composition.

Blue is the color of the sky and water, the source of life. In color psychology, blue stands for calm, trust and stability. In a nearly monochromatic work, it becomes even more interesting to explore the color and its possible contrasts: shape meets line, color meets non-color, light meets dark.

I started two works in parallel this way. During the process, both developed into independent pieces, even though they could definitely be shown together (find the 1st in another post).

When brothers Luck and Sage Cruz step onto the mats at the Abu Dhabi Combat Club Youth World Championships in August 2026, they won’t just be competing for medals. They’ll be carrying the hopes of Guam.

The ADCC World Championships is the most prestigious stage in submission grappling, and invitations are granted to only the top 24 youth competitors in the world.

Out of thousands of kid athletes across the globe, Luck and Sage Cruz have been recognized among the elite few.

For two kids from Guam, the road to glory has been paved with sweat, sacrifice, and an unshakable belief that greatness can come from anywhere.

At just 13, Sage is the former #1 ranked youth athlete in the ADCC global rankings.

His younger brother, 11-year-old Luck, sat at #5.

Together, the Cruz brothers have captured more than 20 gold medals across Brazilian jiu jitsu, wrestling, and MMA youth competitions in 2025, proving they are among the toughest and most versatile young fighters in the world.

But behind the victories are countless unseen hours. Early mornings before school. Late nights drilling after homework. Weekend tournaments across oceans.

“Hard work pays off,” Luck said simply. “Every early morning and late night of training is for moments like this—when you get the chance to prove yourself against the best in the world.”

Sage, who has quickly become a symbol of pride for Guam’s youth, sees his journey as bigger than himself.

“Guam kids can be the best in the world if we stay disciplined and keep believing,” he said. “We’re proof that it doesn’t matter where you come from—if you work hard enough, you can make your dreams real.”

The brothers train with Atos Guam and Island Jiu Jitsu Honolulu, where their coaches and teammates have become family.

They also lean on the unwavering support of sponsors like Crowns Guam, Cold Stone Air, and Riot Jiu Jitsu—businesses that believe in their mission to represent the Pacific Islands at the highest levels of combat sports.

- "Mamááá, llegaré tarde que igual ligo".

- "¡Uy  per-do-ne, Ro-bert Red-ford!"

Eso es lo que fue Roberto, un guaperas. Uno que tenía un trigal de Wyoming por testa. 

Tú te compras docena y media de Farandoles y no alcanzas semejante fulgor.

Se licencia en Bellas Artes  pero empieza a currar en la tele para sacarse unos cuartos y corriendo el riesgo de convertirse en el típico chulazo a lo Tab Hunter o Robert Wagner. De esos que sí, pero no. De esos que se quedan a medio gas.

Pero Rober era listo y, después de salir en chorrecientas series de la época desde "Maverick" a "Perry Mason", decide dar su salto al cine con "La jauría humana", peliculón de Arthur Penn junto a Brando, Jane Fonda, la Dickinson o Miriam Hopkins. Nada mal.

Tras esto ya está en el ojo de Jolibú y repite con Juanita, ya como prota, en "Descalzos por el parque".

Jamás se vio tal mojamiento de bragas y se convierte en estrellón.

A partir de aquí lo más grande: "Dos hombres y un destino", "El candidato", "Tal como éramos", "El golpe", "Los tres días del cóndor", "Todos los hombres del presidente", "Las aventuras de Jeremiah Johnson", "Brubaker", "Un puente lejano" o "Memorias de África". Todo peliculones y muchos gracias a esa década gloriosa del cine yanqui que fueron los 70s en los que se mezclaba crítica social con entretenimiento de manera magistral.

Entre medias se toma un año sabático y se viene a España a vivir con la retoñada (la foto #5, junto a su vecina en Mijas, es mi favorita ever).

Actuar le sabe a poco y se pone a dirigir. "Gente corriente" lo peta y lo gana todo ese año. Le seguirían dos pelis que a mí personalmente me encantan ("Un lugar llamado milagro" y "El hombre que susurraba a los caballos") y dos peliculones: "Quiz Show" y "El río de la vida", donde le pasa el testigo de mojabragas a un joven Brad Pitt mientras él hace lo propio con Sonia (Braga).

Poco más, como suele ser habitual. No hay nada que demostrar, mucho rancho que mantener y te vendes ante un cheque en blanco como la Demi de "Una proposición indecente".

Un tío sosegado, de relaciones largas, iconazo de estilo, ecologista redomado y gurú del cine independiente.

Un tío cojonudo.

Y el pelazo, claro.

Let’s be clear: Tylenol (acetaminophen) has NOT been shown to cause autism. Period.

Trump stood at a podium and told America to be scared of Tylenol—while his administration (with RFK Jr. at HHS) tried to spin “association” into causation. Association ≠ causation. Real medicine doesn’t work like that.

Here’s what matters:
• Major health orgs and global regulators say there’s no proof Tylenol causes autism.
• The largest studies and professional groups say pregnant people can still use acetaminophen appropriately (lowest effective dose, shortest time) after talking to their doctor.
• Scaring folks away from the safest fever/pain option can push them to riskier alternatives—and untreated fever/pain can harm both parent and baby.

Project by B.Arch student Elisa Andretta (elisaandrettac) for David Freeland’s (davidfreeland) Fall 2023 3A Design Studio.

Learn more about SCI-Arc undergraduate programs at the link in bio.

Empty Steel Cladding
CLT panels rise up with CFS panels. Sliding Glass Doors define the transition from the interior to the exterior mesh balconies. The Glass Membrane evidences the transition from one material grid to another. The mesh balconies are freed from the CLT/CFS structural grid. On the horizon, a light steel structure clads against the building’s suggested faces, providing facade apertures that highlight the void. Another independent layer, the roof, sits as a shed on top of the varieties of systems, unifying them with the same sky. The building can be dismantled into individual layers for reuse.

The Steel Cladding structure paints a faceless face, it voices the possibility of multiuse acting both as possible infill space and as structural actor when it reaches the ground.

Through this choice of skin, the facade as a screen that masks is challenged, rather understanding it as a membrane that reveals and provides spatial telescopes.

Situated in the city, this steel cladding blends with the ordinary. From afar, the different thresholds can already be appreciated. Layers of common materials are revealed by what I choose to call the empty facade.

Within such simplicity, the complexity of the structural details gains autonomy. Every gesture is ready to be seen. The emptiness begins with honesty and ends with rediscovery.

米蘭的街頭突然出現一堆透明的蛋，究竟發生什麼事？今天就來看看 Diesel SS26，如何把時裝秀變成時尚版的「飢餓遊戲」⋯

👉🏻 Diesel SS26 沒有傳統的時裝秀，而是在米蘭的街頭散佈了 34 顆蛋：酒吧、教堂、馬路邊都能看到。裡頭則站著身穿最新系列的模特兒們！

👉🏻 只要上 Diesel 網站就會給你一個動態地圖，而所有人都能透過地圖去「獵蛋」 (Egg Hunt)！

👉🏻 這場比賽吸引 5000 人參賽，而最快搜集完所有蛋的人則能獲得 Diesel 訂製的服裝和包款作為獎品！

👉🏻 這就讓人想到 Glenn Martens 這個月在訪談中提到的「時尚變成了『飢餓遊戲』」的言論！

👉🏻 透過 Diesel 他試圖打破「時尚只服務部份人」的天花板，讓所有人都能參與，不分性別、年齡、職業！

👉🏻 同時他也不忘 Diesel 的核心：翻轉丹寧。緞面的丹寧、印花皮革、解構大衣，持續在服裝設計上突破！

Glenn Martens 在不壓縮深度與細節的理想上，用充滿實驗性的方式說故事，同時讓每一個人都能享受時尚。他說「Diesel 談的是民主，它的本質是一個生活品牌。」這個理想，就貫徹著他的每一個決策。

Perché trovare un jeans giusto sembra sempre più difficile?

Comprare un jeans dovrebbe essere semplice, e invece è un esercizio di pazienza.
Online non puoi capire come cade, come accompagna i movimenti, come dialoga con le scarpe. E per essere certa che almeno un paio funzioni, spesso dovresti ordinarne almeno 10.

In negozio, il tempo è poco, le luci non aiutano e finiamo per provarlo solo con le calzature che abbiamo addosso in quel momento. Per poi non sapere come sta con le altre.

➡️ A complicare le cose ci si mettono le differenze di brand, di fit, di lavaggi: quello che sembra perfetto in camerino, spesso a casa delude. Così negli armadi si accumulano jeans “quasi giusti”, indossati solo quando non ci sono alternative migliori.

Eppure basterebbe osservare pochi elementi chiave – cavallo, orlo, tasche – per evitare la maggior parte di questi errori.

➡️ E poi c’è un dettaglio che raramente consideriamo: la composizione. 
Un denim senza elastane ha una resa migliore, mantiene la forma, dura di più. E ha un fitting migliore, c’è poco da fare. Quell’effetto elasticizzato all’inizio sembra più comodo, ma col tempo cede, si deforma, crea piccole onde dove la linea dovrebbe restare netta.

La verità è che non serve comprare di più, ma scegliere con più attenzione. 
Osservare i dettagli che fanno la differenza. 
Camminare, sedersi, piegarsi. 

Perché un jeans non deve solo “stare bene” davanti allo specchio: deve funzionare nella vita reale.

Nuovo dress code a scuola: davvero il problema sono le caviglie?
Possiamo dircelo senza giri di parole: la crociata sui centimetri di pelle è il modo più pigro per far finta di parlare di educazione. A chi serve? A chi controlla i corpi, non a chi deve imparare.

Polemica sì, ma con logica:

Se “decoro” è la parola d’ordine, valga per tuttə: studenti, docenti, staff. La prima cosa da dire che o c'è coerenza o è solo moralismo.

E parliamo di “Concentrazione”: chi si distrae per una spalla scoperta ha bisogno di educazione all’attenzione, non di regole da collegio 1950.

Infine, lo sappiamo tutti chi viene fermato più spesso al corridoio. Se il regolamento colpisce soprattutto le ragazze qua stiamo parlando di polizia del corpo.

Per il resto sono d'accordo sul fatto che la scuola deve insegnare responsabilità, contesto, rispetto—non far passare il messaggio che la colpa è del tuo top.
Vuoi davvero migliorare il clima d’aula? Parla di come si sta insieme: linguaggio, confini, ascolto, uso dei telefoni, puntualità.
E le regole ci vogliono? Sì: poche, chiare, co-create, misurate sul benessere e la sicurezza, non sulla vergogna.

Io scelgo una scuola che educa la testa, non che misura l’orlo.

(però diciamocelo: alcune persone si vestono in modo poco opportuno...)

Statement from HRC US President David Salters on the passing of former HPD President Robert Clarke.

“I would like to give our thoughts and prayers to Robert Clarke and his family, Robert sadly passed away this weekend.

“Robert was a driving force at Honda Performance Development—he was literally badge #1 at HPD in 1993 and ultimately served as the third president of the organization. He and all of our other magnificent presidents built what is now Honda Racing Corporation USA into a world class racing organization. He is one of the giants whose shoulders we stand on today as HRC US.

“From a personal note, when I became President, I felt I was completely unqualified for leading such a prestigious organization. It weighed heavily on me. Robert, along with all the other presidents, coached and mentored me. It was important to him and he freely gave his time and advice at a local restaurant at lunch times to educate and advise me. I am forever grateful for this as it gave me the tools and the confidence to grow into the heavy responsibility of leading Honda’s US racing organization and empowering our magnificent associates to show the challenging spirit of Honda through our racing. Thank you, Robert, you were an inspiration and a brilliant mentor. On behalf of all our racing associates past and present, we will miss you dearly.”

📸La conservación de las aves y el talento fotográfico colombiano se hicieron sentir en la más reciente edición de los Premios de Fotografía Audubon 2025, donde cuatro fotógrafos colombianos, entre ellos un bugueño de 14 años, fueron reconocidos entre miles de participantes internacionales.

🇨🇴Los galardonados fueron Luis Alberto Peña, Camilo Sanabria Grajales, Cristian Valencia y Shamir Shah, quienes se destacaron en distintas categorías con imágenes que, según el jurado, combinan destreza técnica, sensibilidad artística y un fuerte mensaje de conservación.

🏙️ Shah se llevó el premio en Aves en el Paisaje, Colombia, por su retrato de loros jaboneros (Blue-headed Parrots) en Cali, integrados al verdor de la vegetación. (Foto #2)

🐦Sanabria, por su parte, ganó el Premio Juventud gracias a la extraordinaria captura de un Blackburnian Warbler (reinita gorginaranja) cazando una polilla. (Foto #3)

🌺Valencia fue reconocido en la categoría Plantas para las Aves, Colombia, con una fotografía de un colibrí Purple-backed Thornbill alimentándose de flores nativas en los bosques de Villamaría, Caldas. (Foto #4)

🦅Finalmente, Peña obtuvo el Premio Conservación con una impactante fotografía de un gavilán cerca de un incendio auto provocado en una zona rural de Cúcuta. (Fotos #1 y 5)

Foto: www.audubon.org

The 49ers may be cursed.

With Nick Bosa out for the season with a torn ACL, the 3-0 Niners are in a tough spot.

And this is nothing new to them.

Through Week 3, they've already dealt with injuries to Brock Purdy, George Kittle, and Jauan Jennings. And Brandon Aiyuk still hasn't played yet.

Take a look at their injury rankings the past few years, and where they ended up (per Warren Sharp):

🔸 2024: #1 most injured
🔸 Record: 6-11

🔸 2023: #29 most injured 
🏆 Record: 12-5, lost SB

🔸 2022: #9 most injurered
🔸 Recrod: 13-4, lost NFCCG

🔸 2021: #3 most injured
🔸 Record: 10-7, lost NFCCG

🔸 2020: #1 most injured
🔸 Record: 6-10

🔸 2019: #6 most injured 
🏆 Record: 13-3, lost SB

🔸 2018: #4 most injured
🔸 Record: 4-12

The 49ers have had the pieces to get it done, and have All-Pro talent all over their roster.

But they've been one of the most injured teams, if not THE most, in the past 7 years.

The one year they didn't have injury problems, in 2023, they took the Chiefs to OT in the Super Bowl.

Now, they're looking at yet another season marred by injuries. 

And one has to wonder - are they actually cursed?

Sharing the court with RogerFederer, the greatest of all time and my favourite tennis player since I was a kid, was a literal dream come true. It was an incredible day of doubles with Roger and TommyHaasOfficial on one of the most beautiful courts I have ever stepped foot on.

I told Roger that the first tennis match I ever went to was when my dad took me to the Rogers Cup in Toronto in 2006 to watch him play Gasquet in the final. Roger remembered the match immediately - it was a close one where Gasquet won the first set and had several break opportunities in the second before Roger rallied to win in three. That day solidified my love for tennis (and for Federer), and I’m still pinching myself that I got the opportunity to play with (and against) a world number one and number two! I told Roger that I’ve had actual dreams about this, and his response was “Was this match better or worse than the one in your dreams?” 😂

Roger and Tommy, thank you both so much for your kindness, graciousness, for all the tips and for an awesome match! This is a memory I will cherish forever. I also appreciate your patience with my relentless rush to volley everything. I’m glad Tommy and I pulled out the hard-fought win there on match point hahaha. 🏆🎾

What’s your favorite song from this modern-day classic? 👇🏾

10 years ago today, Bryson Tiller released his debut album T R A P S O U L.

This was the project that shifted the sound of R&B in the mid-2010s. Before T R A P S O U L, R&B and hip-hop were already blending, but Tiller’s take gave the fusion a new identity. He took moody, atmospheric production, added sharp lyrical storytelling, and layered it with vocals that moved between rapping and singing. The result was a lane that artists are still trying to occupy a decade later.

The breakthrough single Don’t spread like wildfire online before the album even dropped. By the time the full project arrived, fans already knew they were hearing something fresh. Songs like Exchange and Sorry Not Sorry showed the vulnerability and rawness in his pen, while Overtime and Rambo carried the grit and confidence that made him more than just a singer. The balance between those energies became the heart of the album’s appeal.

Bryson’s delivery gave every track weight. His voice could sound wounded, reflective, and defiant all within the same verse. That emotional honesty helped a generation of listeners feel like their own late-night thoughts and heartbreaks finally had a soundtrack.

Commercially, the album debuted at #11 on the Billboard 200 and climbed to #8, eventually going Platinum. It earned him comparisons to Drake and The Weeknd, but instead of being lost in those shadows, T R A P S O U L carved out its own space. The record didn’t just ride the wave of moody R&B — it defined the wave.

Ten years later, the influence of T R A P S O U L is everywhere, from the sound of streaming-era R&B to the aesthetics of artists who came after. It turned Bryson Tiller from a Louisville kid uploading songs to SoundCloud into one of the most important voices of his generation.

Once a Roman settlement, later a flourishing port, Bordeaux carries its centuries with effortless grace. The city’s boulevards and neoclassical facades earned it the affectionate name “La Petite Paris”—the Little Paris—though today it shines with its distinct brilliance.

Step into the Place de la Bourse, where stone and sky converse in the water’s reflection, and you feel history leaning gently toward the present. Beyond the city, vineyards spill across the landscape, weaving vintners' stories into wines celebrated worldwide.

A UNESCO World Heritage site, Bordeaux is more than a destination: it is a stage where architecture, history, and the art of wine entwine into something timeless.

MEINE TOP TWELVE 👶🏼🫧 Diesen Beitrag habt ihr euch so häufig gewünscht, also kommen hier meine ganz persönlichen Favoriten in puncto Erstausstattung. Es geht immer mehr oder weniger, ist von Baby zu Baby und auch von Jahreszeit zu Jahreszeit unterschiedlich, aber diese Produkte sind hier on high rotation. 

#1 Bodies, Bodies, Bodies – oder Strampler sind gerade an „Zuhause-Tagen“ oftmals das ganze Outfit und kann man nie genug haben.

#2 Selbiges gilt für Musselintücher. Als Spuck- oder Stilltuch, Decke, Sonnenschutz etc. Bei uns ständig im Einsatz. 

#3 Unsere Babywippe kommt überall mit hin. War bei Baby 1, 2 und 3 gleichermaßen beliebt.

#4 Genauso wie unsere Babytragen, unsere beiden Favoriten sind von artipoppe und flybaby.berlin.

#5 Bei uns ist im Bad kein Platz, aber wir lieben unseren schönen Wickelplatz mit Stauraum, der später als Kommode weitergenutzt werden kann, ohnehin. Tipp: Die Wickelauflage Matty von leander.furniture.

#6 Neuentdeckung beim dritten Baby: Der SleepCarrier, der auch in die Wanne des Kinderwagens passt und zur Spieldecke umfunktioniert werden kann. Gerade in den ersten Monaten super praktisch.

#7 Ein Kinderwagen mit viel Stauraum – würde ich immer wieder wählen. Denkt hier immer auch an die Aufsätze für die Babyschale.

#8 Gut für die Geldtasche, die Umwelt und eure Ressourcen: Mitwachsende Babykleidung, die im besten Fall ein Jahr lang passt. Bei Winterbabys lohnt sich außerdem ein Woll-Overall.

#9 Holy grail in Phasen, wenn Ablegen nicht so beliebt ist: die Federwiege.

#10 Super praktisch für die Nacht: Ein Stilllicht, wir haben seit sechs Jahren den Klassiker von reer.germany zum Klippsen.

#11 Unser Stillkissen dient bei uns mehr als Nestchen zur Abgrenzung im Familienbett und zum bequemeren Schlaf und war schon in der Schwangerschaft nicht wegzudenken.
 
#12 Jedes unserer Kinder hat seine eigene Babydecke, in unserem Fall von der Oma gestrickt. Finde ich mit das schönste Geschenk zur Geburt. Im Video: Oldie, but goldie vom Bruder. 🤍

PS: Vieles davon ist nur vergleichsweise kurz in Benutzung und lässt sich daher oftmals fast neu gebraucht kaufen oder auch leihen. Da lohnt es sich zu stöbern!

🇫🇷 Un costume uni c'est joli, mais on a vite fait le tour assez rapidement. Pour tout ceux qui n'oseraient pas porter un premier costume à motif, voici mes conseils pour bien le choisir !

Primo, optez pour une couleur business : bleu marine ou gris. Deux teintes sobres qui feront un très beau fond. Les autres teintes sont plus osées, elles sont destinées aux aventuriers ou aux paons.

Deuxio, prenez un motif discret, voire ton sur ton ! Cela permet d'atténuer grandement la puissance visuel du carreaux. J'ai choisi un tissu bleu, sur un carreaux bleu légèrement plus clair qui apporte du contraste, sans être trop marqué. Il sera invisible de loin et discret de près.

Tertio il faut aérer votre tenue tout autour. Optez pour des pièces sobres et classiques comme cette chemise blanche et cette paire de richelieu noire. Personnellement je n'aime pas les cravates unies, mais ça serait la solution idéale si vous souhaitez rester discret.

Vous appréciez ma tenue ? Dites moi tout en commentaire !

🇬🇧 A plain suit is nice, but you quickly get bored with it. For anyone who wouldn't dare wear a patterned suit for the first time, here are my tips for choosing the right one!

First, opt for a business colour: navy blue or grey. These two understated shades make a great backdrop. Other colours are more daring and are intended for adventurers or peacocks.

Secondly, choose a discreet pattern, or even tone-on-tone! This greatly reduces the visual impact of the checks. I chose a blue fabric with slightly lighter blue checks, which provides contrast without being too striking. It will be invisible from a distance and discreet up close.

Thirdly, you need to balance out your outfit. Opt for understated, classic pieces such as this white shirt and pair of black brogues. Personally, I don't like plain ties, but they would be the ideal solution if you want to remain discreet.

Tuesday, September 4, 1973. Santiago, Chile. A day to remember: the Third Anniversary of the President Allende UP government. 
Fifty-three years ago the Left democratically voted for President Allende. They’d voted for a better life and won. In the intervening years, life had not been easy: the UP government had Nationalized the Chile copper mines, banks and factories, etc. In retaliation the US government increased sanctions on the country, and many imported items became scarce or unavailable. But in the next three years “El Pueblo” had a little more food on the table, a half-liter of milk daily for every child and a little more justice and equality. Today ‘El Pueblo’ came together to celebrate that momentous occasion: they came by the thousands, by train, by bus, by truckload and on foot. The streets were packed. They were happy. This was their day, their victory, they were everywhere in the center of Santiago: over a hundred thousand people. Together they chanted, ‘Allende, Allende el pueblo te defiende.” Yes it was a day to remember.

🔎 Middle Mesial Canal Case: From Clue ➜ Canal ➜ Seal
Hidden MMCs can make or break retreatment success, this mandibular molar needed careful detective work.

1️⃣ Clues: Wide MB–ML distance and a subtle groove on the chamber floor hinted at an extra canal.
2️⃣ Locate: Microscope + gentle ultrasonic troughing ≤2 mm between MB–ML; NaOCl bubbles revealed the orifice.
3️⃣ Negotiate: Pre-curved #6–10 SS files (watch-wind) + EAL to confirm WL.
4️⃣ Shape: Conservative taper, protect the mesial “danger zone.”
5️⃣ Clean and Seal: Irrigant activation and 3D obturation for a dense fill.

💡 Missed canals = missed healing.
👉 How do you usually scout for MMCs, trough first or hand-file exploration first?

It has been ten years since we first ventured into Colombia. One incident that always comes to mind is our friend’s phone being snatched away as he was trying to make a call. Life was somewhat tougher back then, as the country was still recovering from a devastating coffee rust that swept through the nation. We were standing in the outskirts of the town Popayán, where the Ruiz brothers, Julian and Jairo, had just set up their new warehouse. It was our first time meeting each other, and it was a friendship that has lasted until today.

Until 2016, many of the leftist guerrilla groups like FARC and ELN relied on income from the lucrative drug trade to fund their operations. This inevitably led many coffee producers to switch towards the easier and higher-value coca cultivation. Over the years, we were continually reminded that certain regions were not safe for us to visit due to violence or the presence of the drug trade. Nonetheless, it never deterred us from being curious about this magical country and its people, as we continued exploring regions outside of the usual Cauca, Huila, and Nariño.

This year, we took part in the Subasta por la Paz 2025 (Auction for Peace) held in Bolívar, a small town south of the Cauca department. This was not just another coffee auction; it was a social event focused on farming sustainability and peace-building. Coffee acts as a catalyst, bringing producers and buyers from all around the world together to create a positive and hopefully lasting impact on the many lives involved with coffee. News of this event spread across communities, and producers were eager to submit their fresh harvests for the new year, hoping to land the top spot as the No.1 coffee in the department. The auction was lively, with the entire town and many from surrounding areas joining in to share the excitement and to see who would be this year’s winners.

Choosing to alter the prescribed norm of the physical aspects of SCI_Arc Student's projects was the driving force behind the addition to the campus. It was performed as an Adaptive Reuse project. It utilized three existing lots, upon which currently exist two separate buildings. The main enclosure structure of these were maintained and expanded upon. The expansion fell under the cohesive consortium of roofs, which collide with each other to create the larger vault openings below. These intersection points were specifically suited for collaborative spaces. The main portion of the spaces delineated in the program were given to physical workshops and warehouse style spaces that allowed for the production of life size representations of the projects created at SCI_Arc. This is meant to not just complement the digital work that is created, but rather enhance via the material development and exploration that could be done here.

✨📸 Before you were vibin’ to Bad Bunny, your Mai & Pai were on the dance floor dancing to this mega Marc Anthony album. Yesterday, he closed out Bunny’s concert with his iconic love letter to Puerto Rico 🇵🇷 — “PRECIOSA.” You don’t have to be Boricua to feel that one in your soul ❤️.

I photographed this album cover back in 1994 — a project that opened the doors for me into the Latin music world 🌎. Every track on Todo a Su Tiempo was a party anthem, a salsa revolution, and a soundtrack for a generation 🥁🎶.

👀 Fun fact: Marc’s holding an apple on the cover 🍎 … Not too many people knew that. It was a visual metaphor for The Big Apple 🍏🏙️. Holding NYC in the palm of his hands — and look how it manifested 🔮✨.

This masterpiece:
🔥 Debuted at #1 on the Billboard Tropical Albums chart
🔥 Peaked at #6 on Billboard Latin Albums
🔥 Earned a Grammy nomination + Billboard Latin Music Award + Lo Nuestro Award 🏆

And now, these unseen stories and moments are part of my upcoming photo book 📖✨ — a deep dive into the images that shaped Hip-Hop & Latin music history. Stay tuned, familia 🙌.

When brothers Luck and Sage Cruz step onto the mats at the Abu Dhabi Combat Club Youth World Championships in August 2026, they won’t just be competing for medals. They’ll be carrying the hopes of Guam.

The ADCC World Championships is the most prestigious stage in submission grappling, and invitations are granted to only the top 24 youth competitors in the world.

Out of thousands of kid athletes across the globe, Luck and Sage Cruz have been recognized among the elite few.

For two kids from Guam, the road to glory has been paved with sweat, sacrifice, and an unshakable belief that greatness can come from anywhere.

At just 13, Sage is the former #1 ranked youth athlete in the ADCC global rankings.

His younger brother, 11-year-old Luck, sat at #5.

Together, the Cruz brothers have captured more than 20 gold medals across Brazilian jiu jitsu, wrestling, and MMA youth competitions in 2025, proving they are among the toughest and most versatile young fighters in the world.

But behind the victories are countless unseen hours. Early mornings before school. Late nights drilling after homework. Weekend tournaments across oceans.

“Hard work pays off,” Luck said simply. “Every early morning and late night of training is for moments like this—when you get the chance to prove yourself against the best in the world.”

Sage, who has quickly become a symbol of pride for Guam’s youth, sees his journey as bigger than himself.

“Guam kids can be the best in the world if we stay disciplined and keep believing,” he said. “We’re proof that it doesn’t matter where you come from—if you work hard enough, you can make your dreams real.”

The brothers train with Atos Guam and Island Jiu Jitsu Honolulu, where their coaches and teammates have become family.

They also lean on the unwavering support of sponsors like Crowns Guam, Cold Stone Air, and Riot Jiu Jitsu—businesses that believe in their mission to represent the Pacific Islands at the highest levels of combat sports.

What’s your favorite track from Rahsaan Patterson’s self-titled debut (1997)?

Released on MCA in early ’97, Rahsaan’s first album was a critic’s gem — praised for its honesty, musicianship, and a vocal style often compared to Stevie Wonder. Backed by producers Keith Crouch, Jamey Jaz, and Ira Schickman, the sound was warm and live-leaning: keys, bass, grooves, and space for Rahsaan’s elastic tenor to glide.

Singles Stop By and Where You Are didn’t explode on the Hot 100 but left their mark — both charting on R&B radio and even finding life overseas in the UK. Where You Are first appeared on the Bulletproof soundtrack (1996) before landing here, while Stop By showcased his falsetto power on R&B airwaves.

By the time this album dropped, Rahsaan already had receipts: he co-wrote Brandy’s breakout hit Baby in 1994, proving he could pen smashes before stepping into his own spotlight. And while commercial success was modest, the album built his cult following — heads still regard it as one of the purest expressions of late-90s soul.

- "Mamááá, llegaré tarde que igual ligo".

- "¡Uy  per-do-ne, Ro-bert Red-ford!"

Eso es lo que fue Roberto, un guaperas. Uno que tenía un trigal de Wyoming por testa. 

Tú te compras docena y media de Farandoles y no alcanzas semejante fulgor.

Se licencia en Bellas Artes  pero empieza a currar en la tele para sacarse unos cuartos y corriendo el riesgo de convertirse en el típico chulazo a lo Tab Hunter o Robert Wagner. De esos que sí, pero no. De esos que se quedan a medio gas.

Pero Rober era listo y, después de salir en chorrecientas series de la época desde "Maverick" a "Perry Mason", decide dar su salto al cine con "La jauría humana", peliculón de Arthur Penn junto a Brando, Jane Fonda, la Dickinson o Miriam Hopkins. Nada mal.

Tras esto ya está en el ojo de Jolibú y repite con Juanita, ya como prota, en "Descalzos por el parque".

Jamás se vio tal mojamiento de bragas y se convierte en estrellón.

A partir de aquí lo más grande: "Dos hombres y un destino", "El candidato", "Tal como éramos", "El golpe", "Los tres días del cóndor", "Todos los hombres del presidente", "Las aventuras de Jeremiah Johnson", "Brubaker", "Un puente lejano" o "Memorias de África". Todo peliculones y muchos gracias a esa década gloriosa del cine yanqui que fueron los 70s en los que se mezclaba crítica social con entretenimiento de manera magistral.

Entre medias se toma un año sabático y se viene a España a vivir con la retoñada (la foto #5, junto a su vecina en Mijas, es mi favorita ever).

Actuar le sabe a poco y se pone a dirigir. "Gente corriente" lo peta y lo gana todo ese año. Project by B.Arch student Elisa Andretta (elisaandrettac) for David Freeland’s (davidfreeland) Fall 2023 3A Design Studio.

Learn more about SCI-Arc undergraduate programs at the link in bio.

Empty Steel Cladding
CLT panels rise up with CFS panels. Sliding Glass Doors define the transition from the interior to the exterior mesh balconies. The Glass Membrane evidences the transition from one material grid to another. The mesh balconies are freed from the CLT/CFS structural grid. On the horizon, a light steel structure clads against the building’s suggested faces, providing facade apertures that highlight the void. Another independent layer, the roof, sits as a shed on top of the varieties of systems, unifying them with the same sky. The building can be dismantled into individual layers for reuse.

The Steel Cladding structure paints a faceless face, it voices the possibility of multiuse acting both as possible infill space and as structural actor when it reaches the ground.

Through this choice of skin, the facade as a screen that masks is challenged, rather understanding it as a membrane that reveals and provides spatial telescopes.

Situated in the city, this steel cladding blends with the ordinary. From afar, the different thresholds can already be appreciated. Layers of common materials are revealed by what I choose to call the empty facade.

Within such simplicity, the complexity of the structural details gains autonomy. Every gesture is ready to be seen. The emptiness begins with honesty and ends with rediscovery.

Strap in. Three heady Dark Stars on this day. Here are your September 10th highlights...

1991 / MSG (30 Trips Box Set) - The funk was thick and the jams were deep. I was fortunate enough to have seen two of Branford Marsalis’ guest performances with the Grateful Dead, 3/29/90 at Nassau and this show on 9/10/91 at MSG. Both are among my favorite shows I attended. Thanks to Christopher Hazard c0nund4um for the video remaster 

1974 / London (Dave’s Picks #7) - Contemplative Star > Spam Jam > Apocalyptic Dew

“Unwinding very gently a la 11/11/73, the band circles around the song’s main frame for a few minutes before each member begins to fade into space. The gracefulness between each brief transition is breathtaking as it becomes evident that the sensory intuition level of the band is approaching its maximum facility level. Indeed, as each instrumentalist begins to stray into space, he is met at the destination by his colleagues. Lesh assumes the wheel, and the jam quickly accelerates to jazz mode, complemented by Godchaux’s finest Herbie Hancock “In a Silent Way” licks to date. The band returns to the theme and verse at twenty minutes. After a second meltdown, the “Star” quickly ascends from the ashes into a paranoia jam, a trifle funkier than usual, and certainly bordering on orgasmic. After several attempts to overthrow the playful interplay of feedback screams from Weir, Godchaux and Lesh authoritatively bring the jam to an instantaneous halt. As Godchaux spirals in calculated precision beneath Lesh’s pointed bomb dropping, the jam slowly melts, setting the path for the transition into “Morning Dew.” The Dead ascertain the spiritual conclusion of the voyage.” ~ Brian Dyke, The Deadheads Taping Compendium, Volume 1 (1959-1974)

1972 / Hollywood Palladium ~ A wonderful, long, inventive “Dark Star,” full of pure musical jams, a wild post-verse spacemelt, and a glorious return into a beautiful “Jack Straw.” This performance of “Sing Me Back Home” just may have the best vocal harmonies of all of them. Maybe due to Crosby(?) Either way, this is Church. Don’t miss the “Bird Song” and “Playin’” either!

🍂 THE INTIMACY OF: Autumn in Acadia National Park 🍂 Happy Autumn from Maine! + 🍄‍🟫 share which slide that makes you feel warm and cozy inside! ☕️ 

Ah, my first artworks from this amazing place. I remember it like it was yesterday. Behind the camera I felt so much warmth that day and my favorite thing about autumn each year is the difference they hold. One can be bright and warm and another can be muted and cozy. I create with the emotions of the trees and my own personal, present thoughts of the day. I love how it all feels. Crisp, slightly cool, drizzly…
 
September / October / November are truly my favorite months of the year. My birthday is in September, Halloween is my favorite holiday, and the first frost right before stick season in New England comes in November. All feelings I love dearly.

Growing up in the northeast, I had the joy and privilege to witness autumn in its fullest forms. Red, orange, and yellows creating a colorful cascade along roads and forest tops. The breeze that hits your cheek is a feeling that I’ll crave - always. The cozy sweaters, beanies, and hot apple cider - the smell of pumpkin 🎃 pancakes in my mom’s kitchen. Weekend trips to the 🍎 orchard. I could write a book about autumn (maybe I should?!) 

These images (esp the first one!) makes me feel the warmest hug of autumn the most in my own art collection and hope these images make you feel that way too! 🧡🍂🍄‍🟫 From Maine to Vermont down to my home state of New Jersey, I hope autumn is good to you this year! Let’s make to the best one yet! 🤎

📷 ARTIST NOTE: I hope you enjoy looking at this art as much as I did creating it! Be sure to 🍂 comment 🍂 how these photos make you feel and why you love autumn + grab a print as these are in my shop! 🧡
