Review:

Blake and Dair have known each other since they were kids, and as adults, they’re not exactly each other’s biggest fans. Blair sees Dair as a bully, and Dair thinks Blair is a spoiled brat. But disliking each other doesn’t stop the sparks from flying—and wow, the chemistry is instant and intense.

Finding the One really feels like a redemption story for Blair, who we first met in earlier books with a bit of a mean girl reputation. This time, though, we get to see her layers, and I absolutely loved her character. She’s the kind of heroine I always root for—the underestimated one who struggles with her own self-image, making her growth and glow-up that much more powerful and emotional.

And then there’s Dair. He’s pure KA alpha male, complete with an accent, and trust me—you’ll swoon. The story even throws in some third-act drama, which honestly made me happy because it led to an epic mea culpa and a reunion that had me cracking up.

The family drama is juicy enough to rival a soap opera, and the hurdles this couple faces make their determination to stick together even more powerful. They discover that their true strength comes from leaning on each other. And romance readers, you’re in for a treat—the spice levels are scorching!

If you’re into redemption arcs, messy family dynamics, and a romance that brings both heat and heart, this book delivers.

Project by M.Arch student Vandana Taluru (vandanashekar) for John Enright's (john_enright) Fall 2023 Vertical Studio.

Learn more about SCI-Arc Graduate Programs at the link in bio.

HOUSING RECAST
The project constitutes a critical examination of the architectural typology of single-family homes that gained prominence in the post-World War II era.

Within each 3D print bed, four residential structures are arranged to include one or two bedrooms. The drawings showcase a dynamic arrangement of volumes with walls curving the plan and section to create dynamic interior spaces as well as intimate outdoor spaces. Most walls are shared between units to optimise the quantity of material used.

The 3D-printed concrete walls reach a height of 12 feet, coupled with a dynamic metallic roofing system that envelops and tops the structure. Additionally, the incorporation of pre-fabricated utility pods represents a strategic and logistical intervention in the design. These pods are integrated into the overall neighborhood layout, adhering to a linear organization. This organizational schema serves the dual purpose of optimizing Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) services while mitigating the intrusion of utilityV conduits into the concrete structures.

In addition to these technical considerations, the dwellings are designed to afford each unit its own private courtyard. This feature contributes to the provision of intimate and personalized outdoor spaces for the inhabitants.

Quantitatively, each home is approximately 750sft of built space(Including the utilities pod) and has an additional 150sft of open yard.

Little tricks of „big“ climbs #2: While packing for an expedition these days I start to feel the good old excitement and it makes me think of what were usually recipes for a good expedition in my past. I came to the conclusion that after staying alive and healthy a very important factor was always connected with other teams or better said how to avoid them on the same objective. During my expeditions I always tried to stay away from the objectives I would need to share with other teams. Not because I don’t like people but because I realized that no mater the experience people’s decisions making tend to get more or less affected with other people on the same project. By my experience in a bad way. So my advice for everyone but also a reminder to myself is to be creative and find your peace out in the mountains. As an irony I am sharing photos from trips to Patagonia and India. In case of Patagonia we managed to stay totally alone on our objectives despite being in one of the more busy places in the main season. On the other side in 2014 in India in a very quiet place, we ended up being two parties below the north face of Hagshu with the aim to climb it (even exactly same line). We arrived just a week earlier than the other party realizing we won’t be alone when we were already in the town of Leh on the way to basecamp. We ended up climbing that line and the other party climbed a different one. You can read about a big disappointment and one side of the story in Mick Fowler‘s book. 11 years later I still 100% disagree with it. But this unpleasant situation definitely encouraged me even more to find objectives away from others. There are too many mountains/routes for one life anyway so why putting additional stress with dealing with other people’s plans.

Quais ortodontistas brasileiros produzem ciência com maior impacto científico?

Existem rankings e rankings, é verdade. 
Um dos mais respeitados para avaliar o impacto da ciência é o “c-score”, desenvolvido por pesquisadores da Stanford University em parceria com a editora Elsevier.
📈Essa métrica valoriza as citações que os cientistas recebem enquanto protagonistas de um artigo publicado (1° ou último autor). 
O c-score 2025 foi publicado esta semana. O nosso país apresenta um dos maiores números de ortodontistas entre os mais citados em 2024. São nove, entre oito docentes de universidades públicas de todas as regiões do país: norte (David Normando- UFPA), centro-oeste (Jorge Faber- UNB); nordeste (Matheus Pithon- UESB), sudeste (Guilherme Janson- USP in memoriam,  Daniela Garib- USP , Lucas Abreu- UFMG; Antônio Carlos Ruellas- UFRJ), e sul (Graziela Canto- UFSC), além da Profa Lúcia Cevidanes, atualmente na University of North Carolina.
Produzir e valorizar ciência de impacto é fundamental para desenvolvermos a nossa especialidade e o nosso país. 
Uma ótima notícia para o dia do Ortodontista.

📖 ¿De qué va?
En Lagos, seguimos dentro del mundo del Clan Z: Ness (Vanessa Zakharov), marcada por un pasado lleno de heridas y traumas, se ve obligada a convivir con Lagos, un hombre obsesionado, protector, con sus propias sombras y secretos. Lo que comienza como un matrimonio de conveniencia acaba convirtiéndose en una historia de confianza, deseo y cicatrices que se transforman en fuerza.

✨ Tropes que encontrarás:
🔥 Dark romance con tintes de mafia
💍 Matrimonio de conveniencia
🖤 Pasados duros, cicatrices y segundas oportunidades
🪶 Renacer de las cenizas (como un ave fénix)
🤫 Secretos y giros inesperados

🔹 Lo que más me ha gustado:
✔️ Lo leí en un solo día porque no pude parar, me atrapó por completo.
✔️ Ness me encantó: al principio parece otra cosa, pero pronto demuestra que es una luchadora, una sobreviviente que renace.
✔️ Lagos: obsesivo, intenso, protector… y con una vulnerabilidad que me conquistó (aunque a veces quería pegarle por su enamoramiento de Bailey 🙄).
✔️ Me encantó cómo la autora humaniza a los personajes, incluso los secundarios: todos tienen un porqué.
✔️ Esa mezcla de tensión, ternura y giros constantes que no te dejan respirar.

🔹 Lo que menos:
❌ En algunos momentos el peso del pasado de ambos se hace repetitivo.
❌ Hay secretos que tardan en resolverse y te dejan con ganas de más acción inmediata.

✨ Veredicto final:
Lagos ha sido una lectura intensa, adictiva y tierna a la vez. Jess GR consigue llevar el dark romance a un punto más humano, con personajes llenos de cicatrices que aprenden a confiar. Y ese giro final… no me lo esperaba para nada. Ya estoy deseando seguir con el Clan Z. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️✨/5

"Breach" ya se ha transformado en un nuevo hito para Twenty One Pilots . Además de haberse instalado en el Top 10 de las listas británicas, están celebrando un triunfo mayor en Estados Unidos: su nuevo disco debutó en el Número 1 del Billboard 200, el ranking más importante de álbumes en ese país.

El dúo conformado por Tyler Joseph y Josh Dun logra así su primer número uno desde el fenómeno global de Blurryface en 2015. Desde entonces, sus lanzamientos habían quedado muy cerca de la cima: Trench en el puesto #2, y tanto Scaled And Icy como Clancy en el #3. Ahora, con Breach, alcanzan nuevamente la cúspide después de casi una década de espera. En su primera semana, el disco vendió 200.000 unidades equivalentes de álbum, de las cuales 169.000 fueron ventas tradicionales (CDs, vinilos y descargas completas), un número realmente impresionante en la era del streaming.

Este logro no es menor: se trata de la semana más exitosa para un álbum de rock en Estados Unidos en los últimos seis años. El último en conseguir un impacto semejante había sido Fear Inoculum de Tool en 2019, lo que coloca a Breach en un lugar histórico.

 Según antecedentes recientes, encontramos a Paramore con This Is Why (#2 en 2023, pero sin alcanzar la cima), a Foo Fighters con Medicine at Midnight (#3 en 2021), y a Greta Van Fleet con Anthem of the Peaceful Army (#3 en 2018). Solo casos excepcionales, como Tool con Fear Inoculum (#1 en 2019), AC/DC con Power Up (#1 en 2020), Alabama Shakes con "Sound & Colors" (2015) o más atrás Foo Fighters con "Wasting Light" (#1 en 2011) habían logrado lo que ahora alcanza TØP.

Tyler Joseph compartió la emoción en su cuenta de X con un mensaje sincero y algo sorprendido: “Bueno… Breach fue #1. ¿Por qué esto me puso tan feliz que hasta se me salieron unas lágrimas? No muchas, solo un poco. Hace 10 años ni siquiera entendía lo que significaba un álbum número uno, pero desde Blurryface siempre quise repetirlo. Y nunca llegó. Luego dejé de desearlo y simplemente escribí un disco para ustedes. Para nosotros."

"REVELING IN BLUE #2" | 160 x 200 cm (79 x 63 in) | mixed media, hands and passion on raw canvas.

Swipe for a studio pic, interior example, early stages and some details. 

If you didn't see the post with "REVELING IN BLUE #2" here's a short explanation about the idea I started with:

Paintings come from many different sources of inspiration. Sometimes, like this one, they’re simply the result of enjoying the material and immersing myself in a single color.

My love for the material has always played an important role in my painting practice. That’s why this piece was created mostly with my hands, without using brushes or other tools. I only used them in the later stages to round off the composition.

Blue is the color of the sky and water, the source of life. In color psychology, blue stands for calm, trust and stability. In a nearly monochromatic work, it becomes even more interesting to explore the color and its possible contrasts: shape meets line, color meets non-color, light meets dark.

I started two works in parallel this way. During the process, both developed into independent pieces, even though they could definitely be shown together (find the 1st in another post).

Listening Session: Kind of Blue de Miles Davis
17 de septiembre, 2025

Presentamos una noche dedicada a Kind of Blue, la obra maestra de Miles Davis y uno de los discos más influyentes en la historia del jazz.

El evento contará con la participación de Chema Hernández (chemasoficial), melómano y periodista, apasionado del jazz y colaborador habitual en las sesiones de escucha de Red Luna.

Exploraremos el contexto histórico del álbum: su importancia dentro de la carrera de Miles Davis, la genialidad de los músicos que lo acompañaron y la manera en que definió el sonido del jazz modal.

Después, escucharemos el vinilo en la increíble sala de El Q4RTO, un espacio diseñado para una experiencia auditiva inmersiva.

Esta sesión forma parte de las experiencias de escucha organizadas por Red Luna Producciones, con el objetivo de ofrecer espacios únicos para explorar y profundizar en la historia de la música, permitiendo una conexión más cercana con los discos.

Psycho Circus Was Released September 22 1998

Produced by Bruce Fairbairn. Recorded at One On One Studios and A&M Studios in Los Angeles, CA, January - April 1998. Final mastering completed 6/24/98 by George Marino. Strings arranged by Shelly Berg.  Drums on all of the album's tracks, except "Into The Void," were performed by Kevin Valentine. The majority of the lead guitar work was by Tommy Thayer (apparently offered some $20K for the effort) with some having the sonic signature of Paul Stanley (but not necessarily being by him). Some notes indicate that Bruce Kulick played bass on "Psycho Circus" and "Body And Soul;" and it is likely that there are other contributions by him.

Performance credits:

Psycho Circus - Bruce Kulick on bass; Tommy Thayer on lead guitar
We Are One - Tommy Thayer on bass and guitars; Gene Simmons on acoustic guitar
I Finally Found My Way - Bruce Kulick on bass; Shelly Berg on acoustic piano; Bob Ezrin on Fender Rhodes
I Pledge Allegiance - Bruce Kulick on bass on chorus; Paul Stanley guitar solo
Within - Bruce Kulick on backwards guitar intro (from demo)
You Wanted The Best - Ace Frehley on guitar solo
Raise Your Glasses - Paul Stanley guitar solo
Dreamin' - Bruce Kulick on bass
Journey Of 1,000 Years - Shelly Berg on acoustic piano

** It's pretty obvious that there are other players on the album, mainly Tommy Thayer (providing the majority of lead and rhythm guitars) and Kevin Valentine (drums). The only song on the album the original four members play on is "Into The Void"...

Chart Action:

Chart Peak: #3 (10/1/98) with 14 weeks on charts. Other countries: AUS #25; AUZ #1; CAN #2; GER #5; JAP #20; NOR #4; SWE #1; SWZ #30; UK #47.

RIAA/Sales:

"Psycho Circus" was certified gold by the RIAA on 10/22/98. By February 2007 the album had sold 481,000 according to SoundScan(r). It is currently out-of-print in the USA. By 2003 Universal Music International reported international sales of over 400,000 of the album (Billboard, 8/9/03).

Long road trips with kids don’t have to mean endless screens. We did a 7 hour road trip with our (almost) 4 year old, and here are some things that really helped us:

1️⃣ Save the screen-free travel activities for later in the trip (don’t hand them out right away!)

2️⃣ Pack plenty of healthy road trip snacks to keep blood sugar balanced

3️⃣ Plan movement breaks — kids need 10–15 minutes to run, stretch, and reset before hopping back in the car

Honestly, sitting that long is tough for little kids, but with the right mix of activities, snacks, and stops, I felt it was totally doable. And if you end up using screens for some parts of it, save it towards the end!

New studies show metabolism doesn’t actually slow down with age. So, what’s actually going on?

It all comes down to muscle.

The greatest single influence on your metabolic rate is how much muscle you have. Muscle mass decreases approximately 3–8% per decade after the age of 35 if you’re not doing anything to proactively MAINTAIN and BUILD it.

Age-related muscle loss has a massive ripple effect. As you lose it, you become more insulin resistant. This causes poor blood sugar control, fatigue, chronic inflammation, and hormonal shifts, like high cortisol and low estrogen.

Studies show the solution is simple: protect your muscle to prevent decline.

WHAT CAN YOU DO? As you age, you need to eat MORE protein to initiate muscle protein synthesis. Your body is continually breaking down protein and building new protein throughout the day. 

Women 40+ need an additional 10-15g per meal than younger adults to stimulate muscle growth! Without it, muscle loss is inevitable.

Another key player? Micro movements. After 40, research shows people move less—less taking the stairs, less walk breaks, less mobility work, less chasing after kids. This shift in movement slowly leads to greater fragility, pain, and loss of strength.

Muscle is your built-in defense plan.

If you want to protect your metabolism, brain, and blood sugar as you age, make muscle your #1 priority.

The Batman: Part II

Matt Reeves said early on that every idea was on the table, even Robin. “Well sure you talk about everything. There is probably not any character that we didn’t talk about. What could this be? What could that be? That’s part of the beginning of anything.” A major focus was the villain, and Reeves teased a new angle: “Picking the right villain that digs into his past and his life… I will say it’s never really been done in a movie before.”

This time, the film will lean more into Bruce Wayne. “One of the explorations for me was to do something that pushes even further into the character of Bruce Wayne because the first story is so much about The Batman. I never wanted to lose [Robert Pattinson] at the center of these stories.”

The script has already impressed the cast. Colin Farrell praised it, saying, “The script is unbelievable. It’s so good. God, Matt Reeves, it’s so good. It really is. It’s extraordinary.” Reeves also shared Robert Pattinson’s reaction after reading: “He’s Batman, so if he doesn’t like it, not good… the fact that he did was incredibly encouraging.”

With the script finished, the film is officially in pre-production. Reeves confirmed, “We’re beginning. We’re staffing up. We’re starting to get our crew back together. We’re basically entering pre-production. We’ll be making the movie in the spring… super excited.” He also promised, “I really do think this movie will be better than the last. [Robert Pattinson] feels that way.”

Reeves closed with a tease for fans: “I feel so honored to be preparing to shoot the Next Chapter of our story… Can’t wait to share lots of exciting things about the movie with you all in the weeks and months to come.”

What does it mean to confront the memories of a nation scarred by war — and to find new ways of seeing beyond its silences?

𝘈𝘧𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘈𝘱𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘢𝘴 brings together six pioneering Sri Lankan artists — Anoli Perera (anoliperera ), Chandraguptha Thenuwara (chandragupthathenuwara ), Jagath Weerasinghe (jagathweerasinghe ), Kingsley Gunatillake (kingsleygunatillake ), Muhanned Cader (muhannedcader ), and Pala Pothupitiye (palapothupitiye ) — who in the 1990s forged a visual language that challenged state narratives of power and reshaped how the experience of violence could be articulated in the public sphere. 

In 𝘏𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘴 𝘞𝘳𝘢𝘱𝘱𝘦𝘥 𝘪𝘯 𝘊𝘭𝘰𝘵𝘩, 𝘉𝘰𝘳𝘥𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘙𝘢𝘪𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘪𝘯 𝘍𝘭𝘢𝘨𝘴, Hema Shironi (shironijoseph ) turns fabric, thread, and found material into meditations on how histories, memories, and identities are layered unequally in the aftermath of war. Grappling with her own struggle to locate her lived experience within multi-generational histories, Shironi pushes us to acknowledge many truths of Tamilness and Sinhalaness — tethered to land, blood, and memory — even as she insists on the possibility of hope.

Together, the two exhibitions ask audiences to reckon with Sri Lanka’s violent past while opening space for shared futures.

𝘈𝘧𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘈𝘱𝘩𝘢𝘯𝘵𝘢𝘴𝘪𝘢𝘴 and 𝘏𝘰𝘮𝘦𝘴 𝘞𝘳𝘢𝘱𝘱𝘦𝘥 𝘪𝘯 𝘊𝘭𝘰𝘵𝘩, 𝘉𝘰𝘳𝘥𝘦𝘳𝘴 𝘙𝘢𝘪𝘴𝘦𝘥 𝘪𝘯 𝘍𝘭𝘢𝘨𝘴, presented by Shrine Empire (shrineempire), are #OnView at Bikaner House, New Delhi, until September 25.

DEAR MAMA OVER 370 MILLION STREAMS ON SPOTIFY

2Pac's "Dear Mama" has reached over 370 million streams on Spotify. This occured just yesterday Sunday on September 21, 2025. 

Undoubtedly one of the greatest rap song ever dedicated to mothers. It remains one of 2Pac’s most iconic, celebrated, and referenced tracks of all time. Countless rappers have drawn inspiration from this heartfelt tribute. It offers a deep look into his early life and his honest, genuine bond with his mother. This timeless classic will always remind us to love, cherish, and be forever grateful to our mothers. Mom, you are appreciated. 

2pac recorded "Dear Mama" featuring. Sweet Franklin & Reggie Green in "Studio B" at Encore Studios, 721 South Glenwood Place in Burbank, California on July 14, 1994. According to the reels information, it was engineered by Tony Pizarro together and assistant engineered by Carlos Warlick. The reel was titled "E-8" and consisted of two recorded tracks; "Dear Mama (Main)" with chorus and "Dear Mama (No Lady Mix" without chorus. The original version was produced by dj_master_tee and was recorded at Unique Recording Studios in or around October of 1993.

It was released as the debut and lead single from Pac's third album "Me Against the World". On March 11, 1995 "Dear Mama" topped at #1 on billboard "Hot Rap Songs" and peaked at #9 on the Billboard ”Hot 100” on April 29, 1995. It spent five weeks on chart. The single was certified Platinum on July 13, 1995 with 1 million copies sold by the riaa_awards.
